/-!
# Feit-Thompson conjecture on primes

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feit%E2%80%93Thompson_conjecture)
-/

namespace FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture

/--
There are no distinct primes $p$ and $q$ such that $\frac{q^p - 1}{q - 1}$ divides $\frac{p^q - 1}{p - 1}$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem feit_thompson_primes (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (h : p < q) :
    ¬ (q ^ p - 1) / (q - 1) ∣ (p ^ q - 1) / (p - 1) := by
  sorry

end FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture

reformulations.difference: Wikipedia forbids (p^q−1)/(p−1) dividing (q^p−1)/(q−1) for all distinct primes. Lean exchanges the variable names in the divisibility assertion and restricts to p < q.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write R(a,n)=∑_{i

review.notes: The sole declaration is faithful. Primality excludes 0 and 1, makes both denominators positive, and prevents problematic truncated subtraction. Nat.geomSum_eq verifies that natural-number division gives the exact intended integer quotients. Lean checks established satisfiable hypotheses at (2,3), verified boundary arithmetic, and found no divisibility counterexamples among all 600 ordered pairs of distinct primes below 100. The source's (17,3313) example has gcd 112643 but neither quotient divides the other, confirming that its disproved stronger conjecture is not the statement here. The research open tag agrees with the cited source. No repository files were modified.
